To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

guanidino acetate (GAA), which is a substrate of creatine synthesis in the body, is transported into the brain by a creatine transporter, which is a transporter of creatine in the blood-brain-barrier, and that GAA is also transported into brain cells by the taurine transporter, a transporter of taurine.
GAA is transported from the circulating plasma across the BBB most like via CRT, and that GAA is taken up into the brain parenchmal cells most likely via tautrine transporter and CRT.

the blood-brain transport of guanidinacetate is mediated by a creatine transporter, and the brain uptake is mediated by a taurine transporter, both of which could be the key factor that facilitates guanidino-acetate accumulation in the brain of patients with GAMt deficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transport characteristics of GAA across BBB and in brain parenymal cells in GAMT deficiency.
the transport of G AA across the BBB and the brain parenchyme in rats, and it may contribute to the elucidation of the pathomechanism of GAMT deficiency and other creatine deficiency syndromes.
GAA transport across and into the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GAA is transported across the BBB by CRT and is accumulated in brain parenchyme via both taurine transporter- and CRT-dependent transport mechanisms, which could be a novel mechanism of GAA transport in the brain.
GAA accumulates in the brain via CRT-mediated transport in GAMT deficiency, and the resultant increase in GAA in the brain causes neurological complications.
CRT at the BBB plays a key role in the cerebral accumulation of GAA in GAMT deficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CRT-mediated GAA transport is the key factor in the pathophysiology of GAMT deficiency.

the abnormal accumulation of GAA in the brains of GAMT deficiency patients is caused by both the increased CRT-mediated blood-to-BBB GAA transport and the increased CRT and taurine transporter-mediated GAA uptake into the brain parenchyme.
GAA accumulation in GAMT deficiency is caused not only by the decreased efflux from the brain but also by the increased transport across the BBB, and the increased accumulation in the brain parenyma.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the blood-brain transport and cerebral distribution mechanisms of GAA are not only dependent on creatine transporters, but also taurine transport, which is the first report of the involvement of taurine transport in the cerebral distribution of GAA.
the brain distribution of GAA is determined by both CRT and taurine transporter.
the brain accumulation of GAA is not due to its efflux transport across BBB, but due to its uptake by CRT and taurine transporter in brain parenchimal cells.
